rationale: iter_0 starts from rsm05 (CatBoost rsm=0.5). It is the most BROAD-DOMINANT combine config: it beats defaults at EVERY K (eval @1 0.805 vs 0.695, @3 0.688 vs 0.623, @5 0.639 vs 0.595, @10 0.573 vs 0.535 -- the single best @10 in the whole 18-config set -- @20 0.501 vs 0.507 ~flat), with the cleanest train_val_gap (-0.005, not overfit). This is the broad-not-spiky profile that the +50%/200d cbagent crusher's win was built on (it also landed on rsm=0.5): at H=200 the sweep's default model held eval@1 0.825->test 0.630 BECAUSE it was broad, so the eval->test-robust play is a config that lifts the whole top-tail, NOT one that spikes @1 by collapsing @20. Deliberately NOT picking alpha05 (eval @1=0.845, the highest) or alpha10 (@3=0.755, highest): both buy top-of-book via L1 shrinkage but ERODE @5/@10/@20 below rsm05 (alpha05 @10=0.538, alpha10 @20=0.473) -- the exact @1-spiky over-fit pattern flagged for H=200. eta03 has the best val_brier (0.10425) + best @3/@5 but its @1=0.705 is ~defaults and @20=0.489 is weak -- strong middle, weak top-of-book; since the bar weighs @1 most (test @1 0.727), rsm05's @1=0.805 with broad support is the better start. Will use loop iters to A/B rsm05 vs defaults and probe rsm0.7 / a light alpha addition; best-checkpoint selection across iters (eval R-p@1 oracle, anti_auc_flag='unknown' so I treat eval R-p@K as the holdout signal) picks the genuine winner.
